findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema is invalid and rejects all synced tokens
findings.body: File packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts defines minimumTokenResponseSchema with computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()]. That does not create a catch-all/passthrough schema; it creates literal properties named by Zod's toString output that must be numbers. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the code therefore validates every external refresh response against the wrong shape, strips unknown fields like expiry_date/refresh_token, and will fail with Invalid refreshed tokens were returned. Use .passthrough() or .catchall(z.unknown()) instead.

findings.title: Injects dummy refresh_token literal corrupting stored credentials
findings.body: File packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts overwrites a missing refresh_token with the literal string refresh_token. When the external credential-sync endpoint returns only access_token+expiry, this dummy value is persisted to the credential. Subsequent native refreshes or validations that require a real refresh token will then use refresh_token and fail, and the DB no longer holds the true refresh token.

findings.title: Sync path returns raw fetch Response breaking callers expecting tokens
findings.body: File packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns the raw fetch Response when credential syncing is enabled, but returns whatever refreshFunction returns otherwise. Callers are inconsistent: Google expects res.data, HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object, ZoHo expects axios {data}, while Office365/Webex/Zoom/Lark expect a fetch Response for handleErrorsJson/handleWebexResponse/handleZoomResponse/handleLarkError. There is no .json() parsing, no response.ok check, no Content-Type header, and no auth secret sent, so half the integrations crash or store undefined tokens when sync is on.

findings.title: Google refresh uses res.data on fetch Response and stores Zod wrapper
findings.body: File packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts does const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data. When sync is enabled res is a fetch Response which has no .data, so token is undefined and token.access_token throws. It then does const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials,...) which returns a SafeParse result {success,data}, and stores that wrapper object as prisma.credential key instead of .data, corrupting the credential with {success,data} shape.

findings.title: HubSpot refresh expects token object but gets fetch Response
findings.body: File packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts assigns const hubspotRefreshToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...). In sync mode that value is a fetch Response, not a HubspotToken. The next lines read hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn/accessToken and call prisma.credential.update with the Response object, storing garbage and setting expiryDate to NaN, breaking HubSpot auth when sync is enabled.

findings.title: Passes credentialId as userId and expects axios shape from fetch
findings.body: File packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts calls refreshOAuthTokens(..., zoho-bigin, credentialId) where the third parameter is defined as userId:number|null. It sends the credential primary key as calcomUserId to the external endpoint, so the external system looks up the wrong user. It then reads tokenInfo.data.error/access_token, but the sync path returns a fetch Response with no .data, causing a crash or storing undefined.

findings.title: ZoHo CRM refresh reads .data from fetch Response
findings.body: File packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts wraps its axios call with refreshOAuthTokens and then reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error/access_token. When sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, not an axios response, so .data is undefined and the code throws when setting expiryDate or persists an invalid key.

findings.title: Uses prisma without importing it
findings.body: File packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts calls prisma.credential.update at line 96 but has no import of @calcom/prisma. This throws ReferenceError: prisma is not defined on every Salesforce getClient call, breaking all Salesforce calendar operations after this PR.

findings.title: Checks response.statusText instead of response.ok
findings.body: File packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts does if (response.statusText !== OK) throw. statusText is implementation-dependent and often empty with undici/node-fetch, so successful token refreshes can be rejected, and error bodies are discarded. Check !response.ok or status codes instead.

findings.title: Creates jsforce connection with stale tokens after refresh
findings.body: File packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts fetches new tokens into accessTokenParsed and persists them, but then constructs new jsforce.Connection with instanceUrl/accessToken/refreshToken from the old credentialKey instead of the refreshed values. The client therefore continues to use the expired access token until the next instantiation.

findings.title: Wrong appSlug sent to credential sync endpoint
findings.body: File packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts calls refreshOAuthTokens(..., zoomvideo, ...). The Zoom app slug/appId used elsewhere is zoom (type zoom_video, appId zoom). An external sync endpoint keyed by appSlug will not match zoomvideo, so synced refreshes for Zoom will miss or require a special case.

findings.title: Webhook accepts any method and throws 500 on bad body
findings.body: File apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts has no req.method check, so GET/PUT/DELETE with the webhook secret can create/overwrite credentials. It also uses appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) without try/catch, so invalid bodies throw an unhandled exception resulting in 500 instead of 400, and symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse on line 57 can similarly throw.

findings.title: Non-atomic findFirst then create/update allows duplicates
findings.body: File apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts does findFirst by userId+appId then separate update or create without a transaction or upsert on a unique constraint. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both miss and both create, leaving duplicate credentials. It also stores arbitrary decrypted JSON as key with no schema validation per app type.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is string not boolean
findings.body: File packages/lib/constants.ts defines APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED as process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which evaluates to a string or undefined, not a boolean. Consumers treat it as a flag; leaking secret-adjacent values and confusing type-checks. Coerce with Boolean() or !!.
